_note: Maize mission. Approved wording 2026-09-30. Every step must keep at least one free option (no 'item'). 'best' marks the ideal choice; on a step with 'challenge': true it earns the challenge coins. Yield = baseYield x each chosen option's (1 + yieldPct/100); an option with 'item' uses that shop item's yieldPct.

lesson.en: Farming is a sequence of decisions.

intro.en: Every farmer makes lots of choices. Good choices mean more maize. Let's farm!

prompt.en: Your field is ready. How will you get the soil ready?

reply.en: Compost feeds the soil. Strong soil, strong maize!
Burning is quick, but it burns away food the soil needs.
Hard, hungry soil gives a smaller harvest.

question.en: What does compost give the soil?

explanation.en: Compost is old plants and manure. It gives the soil food that helps maize grow big.

prompt.en: Seeds are where every harvest begins.

reply.en: Saving coins is smart, but your harvest might be small.
Great pick! Good seed means more maize.
Clever! This seed keeps growing when rain is short.

text.en: When the first good rains come (Nov–Dec)

reply.en: Perfect timing! Wet soil helps seeds grow.
Seeds in dry soil can't sprout.
Planting late leaves too little time to grow before the rains end.

prompt.en: Oh no! Caterpillars are eating the leaves!

text.en: Check plants every week and remove pests early

reply.en: Well done! Catching pests early saves the crop.
Pests spread fast. Much of the crop was lost.

text.en: Spray lots of chemicals every day

reply.en: Too much spray costs money and harms helpful insects.

question.en: Why check your crop every week?

explanation.en: Small problems are easy to fix. Checking often means you find them before they grow big.

prompt.en: Your maize is tall! When will you harvest?

text.en: When the cobs are dry and hard

reply.en: Dry cobs keep well. Great harvest!

text.en: Early, while the cobs are still wet

prompt.en: Where will you keep your maize?

text.en: Sealed bags or a sealed drum

reply.en: No insects or damp can get in. Safe maize!

text.en: An open pile on the floor

reply.en: Weevils, rats and damp spoiled some maize.

text.en: To keep insects and damp out

explanation.en: Insects and damp spoil maize. A sealed bag or drum keeps them out, so none is wasted.

prompt.en: Time to sell! What's your plan?

text.en: Keep some for food, sell some now, save some to sell later

reply.en: Smart! Prices are often higher later, and your family has food.
Quick coins, but prices are often lowest at harvest time.
Food is safe, but you need coins to farm again next year.
